text:
jonathan: quick proposal — add a compact 'release_matrix' + 'circuit_breaker' to rollout metadata so ops can express cohort gating, region splits, and an automatic unpin when quality drops. idea is to keep it small and interoperable with dedicated/private deployments.

sam: can you sketch the fields? interested in how this differs from the existing 'pin' + 'hints' we have.

maria: fwiw we need to avoid coupling too many runtime semantics into the control-plane schema. circuit breakers are nice but might be better as observability hooks that trigger a separate unpin workflow.

jonathan: agreed on minimalism. sketch below — not final, just to show intent:
```json
{
  "release_matrix": [
    {"cohort": "canary", "pct": 5, "metric_gate": "latency.p95 < 200"},
    {"cohort": "tier1-us", "pct": 50},
    {"cohort": "global", "pct": 100}
  ],
  "circuit_breaker": {"enabled": true, "metric": "error_rate", "threshold": 0.03, "auto_unpin": "on_regress"}
}
```

eva: I like the matrix shape — it's expressive. question: how do we represent tenant overrides (customer pins) vs platform rollouts? need clear precedence rules.

ryan: precedence should be: customer pin > tenant override > rollout matrix > default resolver. we had surprises before where a tenant pin accidentally got rolled back by infra automation.

sam: +1 to explicit precedence. also need a soft-expiry/ttl on rollout entries so old matrices don't lie dormant for months.

maria: about the circuit_breaker, instead of embedding heavy logic (like thresholds with every metric name), maybe support a short 'signal' pointer to an alert policy id managed by telemetry. control plane just stores the id and 'auto_unpin' boolean. keeps schema stable.

jonathan: good call. change proposal: circuit_breaker.metric -> circuit_breaker.alert_policy_id. examples: "ap-1234". the alert policy defines thresholds and lookback windows.

ryan: operationally, we need to record the reason and snapshot when an auto_unpin occurs: model id, rollout id, metric values, and which fallback was chosen. add lightweight fields for that in the rollout audit record, not the primary schema.

eva: also add a 'grace_window' so small blips don't trigger immediate unpins. 5m-15m seems reasonable defaults.

jonathan: updated minimal fields:```json
{
  "release_matrix": [{"cohort":"canary","pct":5}],
  "circuit_breaker": {"enabled": true, "alert_policy_id": "ap-1234", "auto_unpin": "on_regress", "grace_window_secs": 600},
  "ttl_secs": 2592000
}
```

sam: sounds good. one more tradeoff: should we allow multiple fallback strategies in the schema (e.g., pin -> fallback_model -> degrade_mode)? or keep fallback as an ops-only playbook?

maria: prefer a single 'fallback_model' string in metadata for deterministic behavior. complex strategies should live in the runtime config attached to an environment.

deploy-bot: INFO: canary rollout triggered for model: redwood/gptx-11b@v3 by jonathan at 3478901234. cohorts: canary(5%), tier1-us(50%).

jonathan: next steps — I'll update the RFC PR with the compact schema, include alert_policy_id approach, add precedence docs and TTL guidance. maria/sam/ryan — can one of you volunteer to write the small ops runbook for auto_unpin behavior (and audit fields)?

maria: I can take the runbook. will include sample incident playbook and manual-rollback steps.

ryan: i'll add the precedence section to the PR and a couple of unit tests for resolver order.

sam: i'll review the PR and check the SDK serialization for dedicated/private compatibility.

jonathan: thanks — i'll spin the PR tonight and tag you all. :thumbsup:
